title: Good News of Great Joy
subtitle: Luke in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
Luke begins with a young woman saying yes and a baby laid in a feeding trough, and ends with two tired travelers at a table, their hearts burning. In between: shepherds in a field, a net about to break, a lost sheep, a lost coin, a father running down the road, a thief who asks to be remembered, and an empty tomb at sunrise.

This book walks through it in forty short poems, in five parts, beginning with ten poems for Christmas. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture. The pictures stay with the things the story touches—a manger full of straw, a broken loaf, a lamp and a broom—and leave the faces to your imagination.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Open the Gospel of Luke alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

paintings.title: favored
paintings.epigraph: “Rejoice, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you.”
paintings.poem:
she wasn't in the temple.
she wasn't praying on a mountain.

she was a young woman
in a small town
no one expected
anything from.

and heaven's first word to her
was rejoice.

favored
doesn't mean
important.

it means
chosen,
and loved,
and not alone.

paintings.title: let it be
paintings.epigraph: “Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.”
paintings.poem:
she asked one question:
how?

and got an answer
that explained nothing
and promised everything:

nothing God says
is impossible.

so she said yes.
not because it made sense.
because she knew
who was asking.

let it be.

three words
that opened the door
to Christmas.

paintings.title: my soul magnifies
paintings.epigraph: “My soul magnifies the Lord.”
paintings.poem:
she ran to her cousin's house
in the hills

and when Elizabeth
blessed her,
a song came out
that she'd been carrying
all the way.

the proud scattered.
the hungry filled.
the lowly lifted.

she was singing
about a kingdom
that hadn't been born yet.

and she was
carrying it.

paintings.title: the dawn from on high
paintings.epigraph: “because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us”
paintings.poem:
an old priest
who hadn't spoken
for months

opened his mouth
and out came
a sunrise.

the dawn from on high
will visit us.

not because we earned it.
not because we asked.

because of the tender mercy
of our God.

sit in the dark long enough,
and you learn
what morning means.

paintings.title: no room
paintings.epigraph: “She wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.”
paintings.poem:
no room.

not in the inn.
not in the plans
of anyone important.

so God arrived
where the animals ate,

wrapped in strips of cloth,
laid on straw.

he has never
needed a palace.

he still comes
to whatever room
we make.

paintings.title: keeping watch
paintings.epigraph: “There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.”
paintings.poem:
the night shift.

the ones who smelled like sheep,
who spent their nights
out in the fields,

who were awake
because somebody
had to be.

that's who God
told first.

if you're keeping watch
in the dark tonight,

heaven knows
exactly where you are.

paintings.title: great joy
paintings.epigraph: “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.”
paintings.poem:
the first word
of the good news
was don't be afraid.

then:
great joy.
for all the people.

not some.
not the deserving.
all.

there is born to you
today
a Savior.

to you.

paintings.title: the sign
paintings.epigraph: “This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”
paintings.poem:
not a crown.
not a thunderclap.
not a throne room.

the sign was
a baby
in a feeding trough.

that's how you'd know
it was God:

he'd be
where no one
would think to look.

he'd be
small enough
to hold.

paintings.title: pondering
paintings.epigraph: “But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.”
paintings.poem:
shepherds at the door.
angels in the sky.
strangers repeating
what they'd been told.

and Mary
didn't explain it,
or post about it,
or tell it all at once.

she kept it.
she turned it over
in her heart
like something precious.

some things
you don't understand yet.

you just hold them.

paintings.title: now in peace
paintings.epigraph: “Now you are releasing your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation”
paintings.poem:
Simeon waited
his whole life.

and when he finally held him,
he didn't ask for anything else.

not more years.
not a front-row seat.

my eyes have seen.
I can go now,
in peace.

some promises
are worth a lifetime
of waiting.

this was
the one.

paintings.title: the scroll
paintings.epigraph: “He has sent me to heal the broken hearted, to proclaim release to the captives”
paintings.poem:
his hometown.
his synagogue.
the scroll of Isaiah.

he found the place
and read it out:

good news to the poor.
healing for the broken hearted.
release for the captives.

then he rolled it up,
sat down,

and said
today.

paintings.title: at your word
paintings.epigraph: “Master, we worked all night, and took nothing; but at your word I will let down the net.”
paintings.poem:
he was the fisherman.
he knew the lake.

all night.
nothing.

and a carpenter
tells him
to try again.

at your word.

that's the whole
secret of faith:

tired, doubtful,
doing it anyway
because he said so.

the net
started breaking.

paintings.title: through the roof
paintings.epigraph: “Seeing their faith, he said to him, “Man, your sins are forgiven you.””
paintings.poem:
the door was blocked.
the house was full.

so four friends
climbed up,
tore open the roof,
and lowered him down.

seeing their faith—
not his.

sometimes you can't
get there yourself.

that's what friends
and ropes
are for.

paintings.title: don't cry
paintings.epigraph: “When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said to her, “Don’t cry.””
paintings.poem:
a widow.
her only son.
the funeral already
on its way out the gate.

no one asked him
to do anything.

he saw her,
and his heart broke,

and he said
the thing we say
when we can't fix it:

don't cry.

except
he could.

paintings.title: she loved much
paintings.epigraph: “her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much.”
paintings.poem:
the dinner guests
all knew her reputation.

she didn't say anything.
she couldn't.

she just cried
on his feet,
and wiped them with her hair,
and poured out
the perfume
she had brought.

the respectable host
saw a sinner.

Jesus saw
someone
who knew how much
she'd been forgiven.

paintings.title: where is your faith
paintings.epigraph: “He awoke, and rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and they ceased, and it was calm.”
paintings.poem:
he was asleep.
they were bailing water.

master, we're dying!

and he got up,
spoke to the wind
like a parent to a child,

and it was calm.

then he asked them
a gentle question:

where is your faith?

not gone.
just
asleep in the boat.

paintings.title: the fringe of his cloak
paintings.epigraph: “Daughter, cheer up. Y our faith has made you well. Go in peace.”
paintings.poem:
twelve years
of bleeding,
of doctors,
of being called unclean.

she didn't want
to be seen.

she just reached
through the crowd

for the edge of his cloak.

and he stopped everything
to find her,

not to scold her—

to call her
daughter.

paintings.title: twelve baskets
paintings.epigraph: “They ate and were all filled. They gathered up twelve baskets of broken pieces that were left over.”
paintings.poem:
five loaves.
two fish.
five thousand men,
plus everyone else.

he looked up,
gave thanks,
and broke it.

and the leftovers
filled more baskets
than they started with.

give him
what little you have.

he always
gives back
more.

paintings.title: the Samaritan
paintings.epigraph: “When he saw him, he was moved with compassion”
paintings.poem:
the priest
crossed the road.

the Levite
crossed the road.

and the one
who was supposed to be the enemy

stopped.

bandages.
oil.
wine.
his own donkey.
his own money.

who is my neighbor?

whoever
you stop for.

paintings.title: one thing
paintings.epigraph: “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things, but one thing is needed.”
paintings.poem:
Martha, Martha.

he said her name twice
the way you do
when you love someone
who is doing too much.

he wasn't angry
about the dinner.

he just wanted her
to sit down.

the work
will still be there.

this moment
won't.

paintings.title: keep knocking
paintings.epigraph: “Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.”
paintings.poem:
not ask once
and give up.

keep asking.
keep seeking.
keep knocking.

he isn't
a tired neighbor
who wants you to go away.

he's a father
who wants you
to come back.

the door opens
from the inside.

paintings.title: sparrows
paintings.epigraph: “Not one of them is forgotten by God.”
paintings.poem:
five sparrows
for two small coins.

the cheapest thing
in the market.

and not one of them
is forgotten.

you are counted
down to the hairs
on your head.

you are worth
more than many sparrows.

don't be afraid.

paintings.title: the lilies
paintings.epigraph: “Consider the lilies, how they grow.”
paintings.poem:
they don't
work late.
they don't
check the forecast.
they don't
lie awake at night.

they just
grow.

and Solomon
in all his glory
never looked this good.

consider them.

then consider
who dresses them.

paintings.title: bent over
paintings.epigraph: “He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God.”
paintings.poem:
eighteen years
of looking at the ground.

eighteen years
of seeing feet,
not faces.

he called her over.
he laid his hands on her.

and she stood up straight.

the first thing she saw
was his face.

the first thing she did
was praise.

paintings.title: the one
paintings.epigraph: “When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.”
paintings.poem:
ninety-nine
safe in the fold.

one
lost in the rocks.

and the shepherd
does the math
differently than we do.

he goes.

and when he finds it,
there's no lecture.

just shoulders,
and the long walk home,
and joy.

paintings.title: the lost coin
paintings.epigraph: “Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost.”
paintings.poem:
one coin.

she lit a lamp.
she swept the house.
she looked in every corner

until she found it.

then she called in
the neighbors.

that's how heaven
feels about you.

not a coin
it can live without.

one
worth throwing a party for.

paintings.title: while still far off
paintings.epigraph: “But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.”
paintings.poem:
he had a speech ready.

I'm not worthy.
make me a servant.

he never
got to finish it.

his father
had been watching the road.

and while he was
still far off,

the old man
ran.

you don't have to
make it all the way back.

just
turn around.66

paintings.title: the best robe
paintings.epigraph: “Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and sandals on his feet.”
paintings.poem:
not a servant's clothes.
the best robe.

not a probation.
a ring.

not bare feet like a slave.
sandals.

he came home
hoping for a job.

he got
his name back.

this son of mine
was dead,
and is alive again.

now
let's celebrate.

paintings.title: turned back
paintings.epigraph: “One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.”
paintings.poem:
ten were healed.

nine
went where they were told.

one
turned around.

he couldn't
go on with his life
without saying thank you.

and he was
the outsider.

gratitude
is the road back
to the one
who healed you.

paintings.title: be merciful
paintings.epigraph: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”
paintings.poem:
the Pharisee
had a list
of what he'd done right.

the tax collector
stood in the back
and couldn't lift his eyes.

seven words.
no list.

God, be merciful
to me, a sinner.

and he went home
justified.

the shortest prayers
are sometimes
the truest.

paintings.title: come down
paintings.epigraph: “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”
paintings.poem:
too short
to see over the crowd.
too hated
to ask them to move.

so he climbed a tree.

and Jesus stopped
right underneath it,
looked up,
and called him by name.

not come down so I can scold you.

come down.
I'm staying at your house.

grace
invited itself over.

paintings.title: two small coins
paintings.epigraph: “this poor widow put in more than all of them”
paintings.poem:
the rich
dropped in
what they wouldn't miss.

she dropped in
two tiny coins.

everything
she had to live on.

Jesus was watching,
and he did the math
the way heaven does:

she gave
more than all of them.

paintings.title: this is my body
paintings.epigraph: “This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me.”
paintings.poem:
the night before,
he took bread.

not a speech.
not a monument.

bread.

broken,
given,
passed hand to hand.

this is my body,
given for you.

every time
you tear a loaf,

remember.

paintings.title: not my will
paintings.epigraph: “Father, if you are willing, remove this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.”
paintings.poem:
he didn't pretend
it was easy.

he asked
if there was another way.

he sweat
like drops of blood.

and still:
nevertheless.

the most honest prayer
isn't the one
with no fear in it.

it's the one
that keeps going
past the fear.

paintings.title: the look
paintings.epigraph: “The Lord turned and looked at Peter.”
paintings.poem:
the third denial
was still in the air

when the rooster crowed

and Jesus turned
and looked at him.

Luke doesn't say
what was in that look.

but Peter
went out and wept,

and later
he came back.

so I think
it was love.

paintings.title: forgive them
paintings.epigraph: “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”
paintings.poem:
while they gambled
for his clothes,

while the nails
were still new,

he prayed
for them.

not after they said sorry.
not once they understood.

they didn't know
what they were doing.

he did.

and he forgave them
anyway.

paintings.title: remember me
paintings.epigraph: “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”
paintings.poem:
a thief.

no time left
to fix anything.

no good deeds
to point to.

just one sentence:
remember me.

and the answer
wasn't someday.
it wasn't maybe.

today.
with me.
in Paradise.

it is never
too late
to ask.

paintings.title: into your hands
paintings.epigraph: “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!”
paintings.poem:
the last words
weren't a cry of defeat.

they were
a line from the psalms,

an old prayer
of trust.

into your hands.

he gave his spirit
the way you hand
something precious
to someone you trust.

and in the temple,
the curtain
had torn open.

paintings.title: not here
paintings.epigraph: “Why do you seek the living among the dead? He isn’t here, but is risen.”
paintings.poem:
they came with spices
for a body.

they got a question
instead:

why are you looking
for the living
among the dead?

he isn't here.

remember
what he told you.

some mornings
the empty place
is the best news
there is.

paintings.title: burning hearts
paintings.epigraph: “When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them.”
paintings.poem:
seven miles
walking beside him
and they didn't know him.

he explained everything.
Moses. the prophets.
all of it.

and they still didn't see.

then he sat at their table
and broke the bread,

and their eyes
were opened.

weren't our hearts burning?

he walks the road
beside you too.

sometimes you only know it
at the table.
